window.text: Cloud Native Architecture for Modern Platforms - 21CSE477TFunction as a service ( Faas )
Example: E -Commerce – Microservice and FAAS
•Microservices  = long -running, independent, small services. •FaaS  = event -driven, short -lived, cloud -managed functions.
Microservices Example - E-commerce app
•Payment Microservice (handles payments)
•Inventory Microservice (manages stock)
•Order Microservice (process orders)
Runs continuously, communicates via APIs.
FaaS  Example - E-commerce app for Payment microservice using Lambda
•Function: validatePayment () → runs only when a customer pays. •Function: sendEmail () → runs only when order is confirmed. •Function: updateInventory () → runs only when order placed.
Each is short -lived, event -driven, stateless.
Cloud Native Architecture for Modern Platforms - 21CSE477TModelling: Bounded Context
Real -Time Applications of Bounded Contexts
•Amazon (E -commerce) : Contexts like Customer Service, Order Management, Inventory,
Payments, Shipping . •Banking Systems : Accounts, Loans, Payments, Fraud Detection  each modeled as separate
bounded contexts. •Healthcare Apps : Patient Records, Billing, Appointments, Pharmacy . •Ride -Sharing (Uber) : Rider Booking, Driver Management, Payment, Notifications  contexts.
Bounded Context in Cloud -Native Systems
•Each bounded context → one microservice. •Services communicate via APIs or events. •Example: Order Management service publishes “ OrderPlaced ” event → Inventory service
consumes it.
•Helps implement scalability, fault isolation, and independent deployments.

Introduction
•In a microservices architecture , multiple services work together to form a complete
application. •Example: In an e -commerce app:
•User Service  (authentication)
•Order Service  (manages orders)
•Payment Service  (processes payments)
•Inventory Service  (stock updates)
•For the system to function, services must communicate  effectively with each other.
This is called Inter -Microservices Communication .
Cloud Native Architecture for Modern Platforms - 21CSE477TMicro services Architecture: Introduction Concept
Introduction
•Microservices Architecture (MSA)  is a software architectural style  where an application is
structured as a collection of small, loosely coupled, independently deployable services . •Each service is designed to perform a single business function  and communicates with
other services using lightweight protocols (typically HTTP/REST or gRPC , sometimes
messaging queues like Kafka/RabbitMQ). •It contrasts with the monolithic architecture , where all modules and components are
tightly integrated into one large application.

polished.text: Containerization involves packaging microservices into containers (using Docker) for portability. Orchestration is achieved through tools like Kubernetes, which manage containers for scaling, self-healing, and rolling updates. Microservices communicate using REST, gRPC, or messaging queues such as Kafka or RabbitMQ. Each microservice typically has its own database schema, and event sourcing or CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) is used when necessary. Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines are implemented using tools like Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI, along with automated testing and rolling deployments.

polished.text: Microservices are a software architectural style where an application is structured as a collection of small, loosely coupled, independently deployable services. Each service is designed to perform a single business function and communicates with other services using lightweight protocols such as HTTP/REST or gRPC. For example, in a microservices architecture, the User Service might use MongoDB for its database, while the Payment Service might use MySQL. In a microservices architecture, multiple services work together to form a complete application, with each service handling a specific function. For instance, in an e-commerce application, there might be User Service for authentication, Order Service for managing orders, Payment Service for processing payments, and Inventory Service for stock updates.
